scope: Selected primary sections and original design proposals; no wholesale standards conformance or copied upstream schemas.

sources.claim: Invalidation concerns an entity's availability after an event.
sources.decision: Align source representation availability. The inference that this must not retire every business referent is our design decision.
sources.limits: No PROV-CONSTRAINTS or complete encoding conformance reviewed.

sources.edition: Moving official page; changelog includes protocol v0.19.0 dated 2025-10-10
sources.section: State & Checkpointing; State & the Whole Sync; Schema Mismatches; changelog
sources.claim: Source state alone is insufficient for safe progress; destination confirmation matters. State is opaque outside its producer.
sources.decision: Adopt local receipt-linked progress shape, not Airbyte message schemas. Reject silent loss of mapped fields in this closed contract.
sources.limits: No live connector compliance tested. Claude's older changelog interpretation is not adopted as the current page version. Stream/global extension remains outside first release.

sources.edition: Moving official page; last updated 2025-04-30 observed
sources.section: State tokens; replay; synchronization reset; removed resources
sources.claim: Tokens are opaque and query-qualified; clients must handle repeated changes and resets. Removal meanings and lifetimes are resource-specific.
sources.decision: Keep scope and epoch explicit; do not infer business-object death or record reincarnation from reset.
sources.limits: No universal TTL or resource-specific deletion contract is imported.

sources.section: Snapshots; Replica identity; Primary key updates; delete/tombstone events; selected pgoutput limitation
sources.claim: A primary-key update is described using old-key delete/new-key create with linking headers. Before-image visibility depends on replica identity; tombstones support log compaction.
sources.decision: Record key changes separately from business identity and source-instance generation. Never invent missing before-values.
sources.limits: Full connector, failure behavior and plugin-specific behavior were not independently audited. No claimed normative contradiction about tombstones is adopted; configuration controls their emission.

sources.section: Entire rendered specification body: input/output, RECORD, SCHEMA, STATE, versioning
sources.claim: Tap state semantics are producer-defined; the specification describes source messages and does not define this contract's destination receipt protocol.
sources.decision: Use as an alternative approach comparison; do not treat source STATE as proof of destination commitment.
sources.limits: No conclusion about all Singer targets, orchestrators or deployment guarantees follows.

sources.edition: RFC 7643, September 2015; page names later updates
sources.claim: Provider id and client externalId have different authority, stability and uniqueness scopes.
sources.decision: Separate qualified source identity from client mapping identifiers.
sources.limits: Selected original section only. Later RFC 9865 and RFC 9967 titles were opened, not their full specifications; no current whole-SCIM conformance.

sources.edition: Moving official documentation; page published 2026-09-10 observed
sources.claim: Connector-defined partition/offset information and persistent runtime configuration have an operational role distinct from business mappings.
sources.decision: Keep installations and progress separate from subjects and authority.
sources.limits: No full Kafka KIP or exactly-once audit; the provider's broader delivery claims are not independently ratified here.

sources.claim: One writer operates at a time; BEGIN IMMEDIATE obtains a write transaction and may encounter contention. Errors require explicit transaction handling.
sources.decision: Propose one local transaction for head/fence checks and durable receipt metadata.
sources.limits: This does not establish distributed leases, authentic host identity, external evidence durability or performance.

sources.section: Introduction and stated rollback-mode scope; hardware assumptions opening
sources.claim: Atomic commit depends on storage behavior; the described mechanism is for rollback journal mode, with WAL treated separately.
sources.decision: State storage/flush and local-host limits explicitly.
sources.limits: Full hardware/failure sections and WAL mechanism were not read in this pass. No unconditional durability claim.

unverifiedSuggestions: Data Vault/MDM school-level suggestions in Claude's S0 are prior knowledge, not adopted normative evidence.
Provider-reported hashes are distinguished from independent host retrieval hashes.
Source content is referenced in original summaries; no upstream schema or vocabulary copied into the implementation.
